title: Nightly job scheduler: rounds, retries and skip cascade
scenario: Replay one night of a batch job scheduler: jobs run in rounds of `workers` by priority (higher number = more urgent), failed attempts are retried up to max_retries, dead jobs skip their dependents, and Test 3 summarises attempts and busy time.

verified.why_correct: The slash format is `%d/%m/%Y`, which looks swapped to anyone used to US dates, but the README says the slash format is day/month/year. It covers exactly the three listed formats.

bugs.title: Blank depends_on becomes a dependency on ""
bugs.old: return [norm_id(part) for part in clean(text).split(sep) if part.strip()]
bugs.symptom: Every test file fails. Test 1: rounds is [] (test_first_round raises IndexError). Test 2: every job is pending with 0 attempts, no dead jobs, J09/J10 pending. Test 3: counts show pending 12, total_attempts 0, mean_attempts None, busy_minutes 0.0.
bugs.why: `"".split(";")` returns `[""]`, not `[]`. Every job with a blank depends_on now waits for a job with id "", which never succeeds, so no root job is ever ready and nothing runs.
bugs.unblocks: Test 1 (rounds appear at all) and most of Test 2.
hints: No job runs at all. Which jobs should be ready in round 1, and what do they depend on?
Look at how depends_on is turned into a list of ids.
split_ids keeps empty parts; filter them with `if part.strip()`.
probes: What does `"".split(";")` return, and why is it different from `"".split()`?
Why does `all(...)` over an empty dependency list make a job ready?

bugs.title: "false"/"no" parsed as enabled
bugs.symptom: Test 1: disabled J12 and J13 are scheduled (first round ['J05', 'J12'], then J13) and appear in the jobs table. Test 2: finished rounds shift by one and J12/J13 have 1 attempt each. Test 3: succeeded 10, total_attempts 15, mean_attempts 1.25, busy_minutes 86.0.
bugs.why: bool() of any non-empty string is True, so `false` and `no` both count as enabled and the disabled jobs J12/J13 get scheduled and take worker slots.
bugs.unblocks: Test 1 disabled-jobs check and the round layout.
hints: J12 and J13 show up in the rounds. What does jobs.csv say about them?
Look at how the `enabled` column is interpreted.
parse_bool returns bool(text); it should return text.lower() in TRUTHY.
probes: Why does a blank `enabled` cell still count as enabled after the fix?
Why did J12 and J13 jump to the front of the queue?

bugs.title: Priority sorted least urgent first
bugs.old: return sorted(ready, key=lambda j: (-j.priority, j.submitted_at, j.job_id))
bugs.new: return sorted(ready, key=lambda j: (j.priority, j.submitted_at, j.job_id))
bugs.symptom: Test 1: first round is ['J03', 'J02'] instead of ['J05', 'J02'] and the later rounds are reshuffled. Test 2: test_all_jobs fails on finished_round values (e.g. J03 finishes in round 2, J04 in round 5). Test 3 still passes.
bugs.why: The README says a higher priority number is more urgent, but the sort key is ascending, so the least urgent ready jobs take the worker slots first. The comment above still says 'most urgent first'.
bugs.unblocks: Test 1 rounds and the finished_round values in Test 2.
hints: Round 1 should start with J05 (priority 9). What does it start with?
Look at the ordering of ready jobs in scheduler.py.
probes: Why does J03 still run in the first rounds even though it has priority 3?
How would you change this if the convention were 1 = most urgent?

bugs.title: One retry too many
bugs.symptom: Test 1: an extra round ['J09', 'J10'] appears. Test 2: only J05 is dead (with 2 attempts), J07 succeeds on a third attempt, and J09/J10 run and succeed instead of being skipped. Test 3: succeeded 11, dead 1, skipped 0, total_attempts 17, mean 1.42, busy_minutes 114.7.
bugs.why: retries_left is already the number of retries still allowed after this attempt; `>= 0` lets a job with zero retries left run once more, so jobs get max_retries + 2 attempts. J07 then succeeds on its third attempt and never dies.
bugs.unblocks: Test 2 dead jobs and attempts; exposes B5.
hints: J05 has max_retries 0 but was attempted twice. How many attempts should it get?
Look at how the code decides a failed job may run again.
probes: Work through retries_left for J07 after each attempt. When should it hit zero?
Why did J09 and J10 run while this was present?

bugs.title: Skip cascade stops after the first dependent
bugs.symptom: Only visible after B4 is fixed. Test 2: J10 stays pending instead of skipped (J09 is skipped). Test 3: counts show skipped 1 and pending 1. Test 1 is unaffected.
bugs.why: The return inside the loop ends the scan after the first dependent, so when J07 dies only J09 is skipped and J10 is left pending forever.
bugs.unblocks: Test 2 skipped jobs and the pending count in Test 3.
hints: J10 depends only on J07, which is dead. Why is J10 still pending?
Look at the function that marks dependents of a dead job.
Don't return inside the loop; extend `skipped` and keep scanning.
probes: Why was this invisible until the retry limit was fixed?
Which other dead job went through this code, and why didn't it show the problem?

bugs.title: Mean attempts floored
bugs.old: "mean_attempts": round(total_attempts / len(ran), 2) if ran else None,
bugs.new: "mean_attempts": round(total_attempts // len(ran), 2) if ran else None,
bugs.symptom: Test 3 only: mean_attempts is 1 instead of 1.3.
bugs.why: `//` floors 13 ÷ 10 to 1 before round() sees it, so the 2-decimal rounding never has anything to round.
hints: Look at how mean_attempts is computed.
probes: Why does round(..., 2) not save you here?
What would `//` give for a negative total, and why does that matter in general?

context_qa.q: What does build_report() do, step by step?
context_qa.a: It loads the config, then `load_jobs` (which drops disabled rows and normalises ids), then `load_outcomes`, runs `run_schedule` with `config.workers`, and finally builds `rounds`, the per-job table sorted by job id, and `summarize(jobs)`.

context_qa.q: How does run_schedule decide when to stop?
context_qa.a: Each iteration calls `ready_jobs(jobs)[:workers]`. If that batch is empty the loop breaks; otherwise every job in the batch gets one attempt via `run_attempt`, and if a job just became dead `skip_dependents` is called for it.

context_qa.q: What does load_outcomes return, and what happens when there is no row for an attempt?
context_qa.a: A dict keyed by `(job_id, attempt)` with the outcome trimmed and lower-cased. `run_attempt` looks the key up with a default of `"ok"`, so a missing row is a success.
A property on Job: `max_retries - (attempts - 1)`. It is read by `can_retry`, which `run_attempt` calls after a failed attempt.
In `run_attempt`, to the current round number, when the job becomes succeeded or dead. Skipped and pending jobs keep `None`.

context_qa.q: What shape is depends_on on a Job?
context_qa.a: A list of job id strings produced by `utils.split_ids` from the CSV cell, using `;` as the separator. `ready_jobs` checks each id against the set of succeeded job ids.

context_qa.q: What does summarize count as a job that ran?
context_qa.a: Jobs with `attempts > 0`. `total_attempts` and `busy_seconds` are summed over those jobs, and `counts` covers every loaded job.
